body:
# Tàijí: the restoration, the temple, and the world it opens
Every name in this series was once flattened to fit a keyboard. **Tàijí** is what the evidence put back.

Tàijí has no body and no biography; its 'mythology' is the story Chinese thinkers told about how the one becomes many. The most influential telling is Zhou Dunyi's short prose poem, but it draws on much older Daoist and Yijing material. Zhou Dunyi's Explanation of the Diagram of the Supreme Ultimate opens: 'Wújí ér Tàijí' — the limitless, and yet the supreme ultimate.  From this arise movement and stillness, yang and yin, the five phases, and finally the moral order of the sage.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Tàijí
- **ASCII form:** taichi
- **Meaning:** "Great extreme"
- **Domain of influence:** Supreme Ultimate, Origin
- **Pantheon:** Chinese
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** 太極
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 232 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **太極**. On the evidence, it means "Great extreme".

Strip **Tàijí** to *taichi* and one piece of evidence vanishes:

- **a → à** — Stress on a: the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Tàijí** lives at [/sites/taichi/](/sites/taichi/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/taichi/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/taichi/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/taichi/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Tàijí** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Yoga, Meditation & Holistic Wellness** — The supreme ultimate that became the world’s most practiced moving meditation.
- **Healthcare, Pharma & Medicine** — Prescribed for balance, hypertension, and stress; the slow form as clinical intervention.
- **Philosophy, Ethics & Standards** — The supreme ultimate; metaphysics in a diagram.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Chinese tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Tao Te Ching](/texts/tao-te-ching/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
## The File Continues

This is one of 271 Restoration Files — a second dispatch from every flagship temple in the fleet. The temple's [first dispatch](/sites/taichi/blog/) tells the founding story of the name; the [blog index](/blog/) holds the whole archive.
